title: Your AI Chatbot Is a Mechanic on the Phone (4-Step Fix)
description:
What is a coding-agent session? An AI coding agent (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot agent mode) explained in 60 seconds.
A chat assistant only answers with text you paste, run and carry back; a coding agent works in a loop with tools: it reads files, edits code, runs commands and checks the result, until the job is done.

Chapters
0:00 The problem: a chatbot is a mechanic on the phone
0:18 The mechanic in your garage: the loop
0:39 Why it matters, and the takeaway

The story: a mechanic on the phone can only talk, so you try his fix, start the car and tell him what happened, again and again. The same mechanic in your garage, with tools, looks, turns the bolt, starts the engine, listens, and goes round again until the noise is gone. That is the difference between a chat assistant and a coding agent. The whole visit, every step and every result, is one session.

The takeaway: the model didn't get a bigger brain. It got hands (tools), and a way to check its own work. It can still be wrong, so give it a test to run.

Try it: Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works), Codex CLI (https://github.com/openai/codex) or agent mode in VS Code. Before chat assistants and agents there was autocomplete: the first GitHub Copilot (2021) suggested whole lines as you typed.
